10:52:56 +0530 Date : 9th July, 2025 P.C. :

1. Heard learned Counsel for the Appellant - Mr. Sadavarte who has fairly argued the
matter immediately after it being listed as prioritised case, since this appeal is
pending from 1994 in this Court.
Also heard learned counsel for the Respondents.

2. The Appeal is filed challenging the Judgment and Award dated 01.12.1993 passed by Extra Joint
District Judge, Pune in Land Reference No. 2 of 1987.
3. Few facts necessary for disposal of this Appeal are as under.

The matter is arising out of the Land
Acquisition Act, 1894 ('the said Act' for short).

By the impugned Judgment, 43 claimants as well as
10 objection petitioners had filed claim for compensation.

The subject matter lands of village
Bhosari, Taluka - Haveli, District- Pune were 2-Fa-211-1994 prio C.doc compulsorily acquired for
the purpose of plant development and utilisation in Pimpri Chinchwad new township area for
industrial, commercial and residential purposes.

This resulted into the Reference under Section 30
of the said Act.

The concerned Land Acquisition Officer granted compensation of Rs.43,20,001/-,

about which the said Reference was made.

Under the impugned Judgment, the amount of
compensation

has been apportioned amongst the Claimants and remaining compensation of Rs.
1,35,001/- has been remitted to the concerned Collector.

The present Appellant, being
'objection-petitioner No.8', has filed this First Appeal challenging the impugned Judgment and
Award.

4. Learned Counsel for the Appellant submitted that some of the Claimants had agreed to sell part of
subject matter properties to the Appellant under an agreement to sell (Sathe-khat) dated 19.01.1967.

He points out that under clause 9 of the said agreement, some of the Respondents/claimants had
agreed that if the property is acquired by the Government, they will pay th share of compensation
to Appellant.

5. It is not disputed that this agreement to sell was never sought to be enforced by the Appellant
against the Claimants and the claim is based simplicitor on agreement to sell.

No material is shown
to this Court to indicate that any suit for specific performance has been ever filed by the Appellant.

6. In paragraph 57 of the impugned Judgment, it is clearly held by the Reference Court, after
appreciation of evidence, that Appellant has not established his interest in the acquired lands and
therefore not entitled to get any compensation.

It is settled position of law that 2-Fa-211-1994 prio
C.doc proposed purchaser under agreement to sell does not get any title.

He has no right or interest
in the property, except for seeking specific performance of the agreement.

No suit for specific
performance is filed.
As such there is no basis for claiming compensation.

Section 54 of the Transfer
of Property Act, 1882 provides as under :
"Contract for sale - A contract for the sale of immovable property is a contract that a
sale of such property shall take place on the terms settled between the parties.

It does
not, of itself, create any interest in or charge on such property'.
[emphasis supplied]

7. Learned Counsel for the Respondents has rightly relied upon the judgment reported in Air 1995
Sc 1891 (Sunil Kumar Jain Vs. Kishan & Ors) to contend that agreement to sell does not confer title
and on the basis of mere agreement to sell, a share in the compensation cannot be claimed.
8.

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, since the very basis of claim made by the
Appellant is found to be lacking legal foundation, no fault can be found with the impugned
Judgment and Award, so far as the present Appellant is concerned.
9. In that view of the matter, there is no merit in the appeal and the same is dismissed.

In view of
dismissal of the appeal, all pending applications, if any, are also dismissed.
No order as to costs.

10. At this stage, learned Counsel for the Respondents points out that pursuant to the earlier order
dated 06.05.1996 passed in this appeal in Civil Application No. 1189 of 1994, certain bank guarantee
is 2-Fa-211-1994 prio C.doc given in the Reference Court at the time of withdrawal of compensation.
